verdict.rationale: Glama does publish quality signals: its scanned/scored registry (91,626 servers, 'every one scanned, scored') and a TDQS quality-score system that a community member praised for helping them improve their MCP listing, plus ownership verification via a claim panel/token. However, hands-on community reports document the score system breaking in practice — a quality-score retest silently failed to rerun for days despite manual resyncs, with the real (undocumented) cause being a missing credit-card/credits requirement, and neither the user nor their AI agent could diagnose it from docs. This is a concrete documented failure of the scoring mechanism working as advertised, not mere skepticism. Missing for 10: clear usage-count metrics, explicit liveness/health-check indicators, and independent corroboration that the score system reliably updates without hidden gating.
